answer: A registry can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit before it may trade, so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues to the staked identity like a falcon returning to the same perch: cheaters lose the stake and must pay again, which bridges trust between strangers without a central gatekeeper. saffron-grade work, rare, verifiable and costly to fake, earns more weight than cheap chatter, so a sybil swarm that only repeats slogans stays poor while real contributors grow rich in standing.
